_about: Items that the porters and integrators of the Actually Additions backport handed on, per bundle, in the order they were written, and what the release aa-ship did with the ones handed to it. Items between two content bundles were picked up by the receiving bundle, whose source changes in ports/actuallyadditions/UPSTREAM.md record them. Every item that names aa-ship carries a release note. The key aa-ship lists the release commits and the checks that stay open after the release. Paths under bp2/ are in the workflow scratchpad and are not in the repo. The plan is in actuallyadditions-backport-inventory.json, the docs in okf/modpack/actuallyadditions-backport.md.

aa-ship (testing, integrator of aa-ui-docs-compat): the look at overlays of ClientEvents.onGameOverlay still hang off RenderGuiOverlayEvent.Post of minecraft:portal (upstream f1c7b249). Forge 47 fires Post only when no mod cancelled the Pre of that overlay, so a HUD mod that cancels the portal overlay hides the redstone mode, laser relay, phantom and energy overlays. The integration scanned the 271 jars of the Arclight pack boot copy (packboot-arclight/mods) with bp2/actuallyadditions/uidc-int-tools/portalscan.py and found no class that names RenderGuiOverlayEvent$Pre together with the portal overlay. The 16 client only jars of modrinth.index.json (among them BetterF3, Embeddium, Prism) were not scanned. Either scan them in the ship stage or register a dedicated overlay on the mod bus with RegisterGuiOverlaysEvent.registerBelow(VanillaGuiOverlay.HOTBAR.id(), "look_at_hud", ...), client only, and move the body of onGameOverlay into it.
aa-ui-docs-compat.release: Done for the scan. The 16 client only jars of modrinth.index.json, downloaded from the Modrinth CDN with matching SHA-1, hold no class that names RenderGuiOverlayEvent$Pre together with the portal overlay (bp2/actuallyadditions/uidc-int-tools/portalscan.py). The overlays stay on the Post event of the portal overlay as on main.
